title: Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance: external address conditions, OR logic and condition testing
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, licensing, condition controls and preview limitations are supported. Minor corrections should expand the abbreviated wizard routes and acknowledge conflicting Microsoft documentation about PowerShell policy management.

claims.quote: our updated policy conditions enable the detection of messages sent and received both to and from external email addresses

claims.quote: we've introduced the ability to test conditions before implementing them. By using sample messages, you can evaluate how your conditions will perform

claims.claim: No separate licence or meter specific to these enhanced policy conditions is published.

claims.claim: Detecting inappropriate or risky interactions for non-Microsoft 365 AI data requires pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: to detect inappropriate or risky interactions for non-Microsoft 365 AI data, you need to enable pay-as-you-go billing in your organization.

claims.claim: Detecting inappropriate or risky interactions for Microsoft 365 Copilot data has no such pay-as-you-go requirement.
claims.quote: There aren't any pay-as-you-go billing requirements or charges for Microsoft 365 detecting inappropriate or risky interaction for Microsoft 365 Copilot data.

claims.claim: The sources do not tie that AI-data billing requirement to using the enhanced condition options themselves.
claims.quote: Searched: Communication Compliance condition builder license billing; Communication Compliance external conditions meter license. Read configure Subscriptions and billing and policies condition-builder documentation; billing is described by AI data type, not by using these options.

claims.claim: Learn recommends the condition builder for new policies.
claims.quote: For new policies, we recommend using the condition builder.

claims.claim: The condition builder supports compound conditions using AND, OR and NOT.
claims.quote: The condition builder supports the OR operator, which enables you to combine multiple conditions in the same policy to create compound conditions with AND, OR, and NOT operators.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn requires membership in the Communication Compliance or Communication Compliance Admins role group to use condition testing.

claims.claim: The condition builder is reached through Communication Compliance > Policies > Create policy > Custom policy > Choose conditions and review percentage > Conditions > Condition builder.
claims.quote: in the Conditions section, above the existing condition builder, turn the Condition builder option on.
claims.fix: Expand the path to 'Communication Compliance > Policies > Create policy > Custom policy > Name and describe your policy > Choose users and reviewers > Choose locations to detect communications > Choose conditions and review percentage > Conditions > Condition builder'. Note that 'Admin units (preview)' appears before 'Choose users and reviewers' if admin units exist. The intervening wizard pages are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/communication-compliance-configure, already cited; the current docs link correctly documents the final control.

claims.claim: No documented automation operation selects the condition builder for a policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Communication Compliance test policy conditions sample messages PowerShell Graph API test conditions condition builder. Read policies, configure, Set-SupervisoryReviewRule and TCM supervisoryReviewRule references; none documents a condition-builder selection parameter.

claims.claim: Condition testing is reached through Communication Compliance > Policies > Create policy > Custom policy > Conditions and percentage > Test your conditions.
claims.quote: Select Create policy, then select Custom policy. ... On the Conditions and percentage page, after entering your conditions, select Test your conditions.
claims.fix: Expand the path to 'Communication Compliance > Policies > Create policy > Custom policy > Name and describe your policy > Choose users and reviewers > Choose locations to detect communications > Conditions and percentage > Test your conditions'. Note that 'Admin units (preview)' appears before 'Choose users and reviewers' if admin units exist. Retain the existing note explaining Learn's differing conditions-page labels.

Read configure testing steps and Set-SupervisoryReviewRule; found no sample-message test operation.

claims.claim: Policies identify communications for analysis by internal or external reviewers.

claims.claim: The sources describe no new automatic remediation mechanism tied to these enhanced conditions.
claims.quote: Searched: Communication Compliance condition builder automatic remediation. Read roadmap, policies, configure and investigate-remediate search excerpts; found reviewer actions and cross-policy resolution after reviewer action, not new autonomous remediation from these conditions.

claims.claim: The condition builder replaces exceptions with NOT conditions.
claims.quote: All exceptions in the condition builder are replaced with a NOT condition.

claims.claim: A NOT condition must be within a nested group.
claims.quote: You must include the NOT condition within a nested group.

claims.claim: Using AND and OR in the same condition requires a separate group for each operator.
claims.quote: To use multiple operators (both AND and OR) in the same condition, you must create a separate group for each operator.

claims.claim: Quick Summary displays a simplified summary of a built condition.
claims.quote: the condition builder includes a simplified summary view of the condition. To see the summary for a condition you built, turn on the Quick Summary option.

claims.claim: Email messages can take approximately 24 hours to fully process in a policy.
claims.quote: Email messages can take approximately 24 hours to fully process in a policy.

claims.claim: Communication Compliance requires the audit log to be enabled.
claims.quote: Step 2 (required): Enable the audit log ... Communication Compliance requires audit logs to show alerts and log remediation actions that reviewers take.

claims.claim: Learn describes testing a pilot policy for several days before wider rollout.
claims.quote: Typically, you need to create a pilot policy and test it for several days before rolling the policy out to the wider organization.

claims.claim: Learn says PowerShell cannot create or manage Communication Compliance policies.
claims.quote: PowerShell isn't supported for creating and managing Communication Compliance policies. To create and manage these policies, use the policy management controls in the Communication Compliance solution.
claims.fix: Add after the PowerShell statement: 'Microsoft documentation is not fully consistent: the Security & Compliance PowerShell reference documents Set-SupervisoryReviewRule with -Condition for modifying supervisory review rules, but does not document selecting the new condition builder or running its sample-message tests.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchangepowershell/set-supervisoryreviewrule?view=exchange-ps. Retain the portal guidance and the narrowly scoped null automation sides; do not infer new-builder support from the older rule reference.
